title: The Duero valley
subtitle: Plateau reds and Rueda whites
objectives: Explain the role of altitude on the Meseta

steps.title: Ribera del Duero
steps.body: Ribera del Duero sits on Spain's central plateau, the Meseta, at 750 to 1,000 m. Tempranillo, called Tinto Fino or Tinta del País, gives deep, powerful reds. Vega Sicilia, founded in 1864, made the name; the 1980s brought international fame. Hot days and very cold nights give ripe fruit with fresh acidity.

steps.title: Altitude and extremes
steps.body: The Meseta is high and continental. Summer days can reach 35 degrees, while nights drop below 15, a wide diurnal range that keeps acidity. Winters are harsh and spring frosts are a constant risk; Ribera lost much of its 2017 crop to frost. Old bush vines on poor soils give low yields.
steps.highlight: Hot days, cold nights, frost risk

steps.prompt: Match each Duero wine to its grape.
steps.explanation: The same river crosses Spain and Portugal, with different grapes on each side.

steps.title: Toro and Rueda
steps.body: Toro, further west and lower, makes very ripe, powerful reds from Tinta de Toro, a local form of Tempranillo. Rueda is the Duero's white wine region, making crisp, aromatic Verdejo with fennel, citrus and herbs, often blended with Sauvignon Blanc. Many Rueda grapes are picked at night to stay cool.

steps.prompt: Rueda is best known for red wines.
steps.explanation: Not true. Rueda is the Duero's white wine region, built on Verdejo.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Ribera del Duero makes powerful Tinto Fino at high altitude
Hot days, cold nights and frost shape the Meseta
Toro makes ripe reds; Rueda makes Verdejo whites
